next_step: Closed-lost follow-up; document lessons learned; re-engage if traffic pattern changes or champion returns
notes: Background: Stratus runs fulfillment and routing for 3rd-party e-commerce merchants. Traffic highly bursty (Black Friday spikes + promotional campaigns). Embeddings used for search ranking across catalogs, chat assistant for merchant support.
Initial interest (2024-09): Eng inbound via solutions form asking about low-latency chat + embeddings at scale. AE assigned (Maya).

Technical discovery (2024-09 to 2024-10): SE Diego ran capacity modelling. Customer requires: p95 < 80ms for chat responses under normal load, < 200ms during bounded bursts; peak burst QPS up to 5k for chat; embeddings workload ~1M vectors/day with periodic 200k/day spikes. Concern: queueing/backpressure during promo bursts causing timeouts and order support outages.

Security & deployment (2024-10): Preference for VPC or on-prem control plane. Strong mandate for audit logs, KMS integration and regional data residency for EU merchants. Security review kickoff (Drive doc link).

POC (2024-11 to 2024-12): Ran 3-week dedicated POC on Dedicated with simulated burst tooling. Results: average latency met targets under steady-state; under synthetic 10x sudden burst we saw queueing behavior for short windows and autoscaler recovery time ~120s. SE notes: autoscale warm pools and pre-warming strategies reduce but don't eliminate transient queueing unless committed over-provisioning used.
Quote from CTO on 2024-12-08 call: "We cannot risk queueing at the start of a flash sale — even brief timeouts cost us revenue and SLA credits."

Commercials (2024-12): Redwood proposed Dedicated + burst reservation option and Optimize recommendations to tune batching/kv cache. Pricing less aggressive than FastEdge competitor for same committed capacity; Redwood offered technical knobs (burst pools, prefix caching) vs competitor pitch of bundled over-provisioned capacity + stronger SLOs.

Procurement cycle (2025-01): Procurement flagged budget freeze in Q1; internal champion (Head of Platform) accepted new offer from competitor who guaranteed dedicated hot standby capacity and an indemnified SLO for peak-day performance. Platform champion left company mid-January — momentum lost.

Final outcome (2025-01-22): Closed-lost to FastEdge Systems. Primary reasons captured: 1) perceived lower risk from competitor's fixed hot-standby guarantee; 2) price savings on 12-month committed contract; 3) internal budget freeze and staff turnover. Security review was not the primary blocker but added delay (still open items in Drive doc).

Lessons learned / internal notes: POC exposed autoscaler cold-recovery as a key concern — we should propose explicit burn-in/pre-warm approach or short-term hot-standby add-on for similar accounts. Sales playbook: surface burst guarantees earlier, provide a costed hot-standby option and a simulation report template for procurement. Consider a standard SLO appendix for burst behavior to reduce perceived risk.
